scenes.title: The manuals are not the problem.
scenes.caption: Reaching them is.
scenes.narration: FEMA, the US Army and Wikipedia publish all of this for free. Reading it still takes a network.
scenes._itemsNote:
Every chip is a document this film shows on screen later, so the card is a promise the rest of the cut keeps rather than a list written for a video. `FEMA Emergency Checklist` and `FM21-76 US Army Survival` are both rows in the FIELD LIBRARY sidebar on the `library-indexed` and `offline-library` plates; `wikipedia_en_simple_all_nopic — Boiling` is the third citation in the `sources-open` plate, which is the frame `check-the-sources` punches into.

The three publishers are named rather than hedged into "reference material", per MESSAGING.md. They are also deliberately NOT the villain: all three publish this for free and the card says so. The structural point is the last sentence of the narration — the document is free and the path to it is not yours — which is the "structural, not moral" framing the blog uses. It states the architecture and stops; `open` supplies the consequence one beat later with "There is no signal."

No number is claimed. There is no outage statistic here because there is no sanctioned one; MESSAGING.md lists the numbers this company may quote and none of them are about networks.

scenes.title: Just In Case
scenes.caption: Emergency knowledge, offline.
scenes.narration: There is no signal. How long do you boil creek water?
scenes._transitionNote: A hold, so the stakes card is not dissolved into the title but answered by it: `meta.holdSeconds` of bare ground, then the mark. The card before it ends on "Reading it still takes a network"; this one opens on "There is no signal." The empty frame between them is the turn.

scenes.caption: First launch. Nothing indexed yet.
scenes.narration: On first launch the library is empty, and the panel says so plainly.

shots.alt: Just In Case on first launch: brand hero, suggested questions, and an empty field library
shots._focusNote:
MEASURED WITH `ci-video focus-preview` AGAINST THE COMMITTED PLATE, 2026-08-12. Widened from 0.538 x 0.5 at (0, 0).

The scene's evidence is three numbers and a sentence, all in the left rail: the `Index empty` pill, INDEX `0 chunks · 0 files`, FIELD LIBRARY `0`, and "No documents indexed yet. Run the content fetcher or drop PDFs into the sources volume." At rest they are 8-11px on a 1080-tall canvas — the narration says "the panel says so plainly" over a panel nobody can read. That part was right and is unchanged.

WHAT WAS WRONG. A 0.538 window anchored at the left edge ends at plate x 0.537. The main pane's hero block sits at x 0.425..0.765 — so the paragraph was sliced mid-glyph along the right canvas edge ("Offline emergency knowledge", "aid, water, shelter, power, c") and the hero JUST IN CASE wordmark, which starts at x 0.540, was cut off entirely bar a sliver of its first letter. A frame edge through the middle of a word reads as a broken render. The window cannot be moved to avoid it: 0.538 is the tightest the kit honours in 16:9 and the rail starts at x 0, so there is no placement that both keeps the rail and misses the hero.

THE FIX IS TO ASK FOR LESS. (0, 0, 0.82, 0.70) -> scale 1.574, honoured exactly, window 0.820 square from plate (-0.001, -0.015). It ends past the hero paragraph's right edge at 0.765, so nothing is cut; the rail is still 2.2x its resting size and every one of the four pieces of evidence is legible in the reconstruction.

h IS 0.70 AND NOT 0.82, ON PURPOSE. The window is square in plate coordinates and its size is set by max(w, h), so h only moves the CENTRE — and the centre matters here because the stage sits above canvas centre by half the caption allowance, which slides the window down. h 0.70 puts the window top a hair above the plate, which keeps the status pill (plate y 0.021..0.037) whole.

PULL-BACK, not push-in. This is the film's first screen scene, so it still owes the viewer a wide establishing read of the whole appliance — and it can have both: open on the rail and the hero together, then reveal the app around them. A pull-back STARTS at the focus, so `ci-video focus-preview --scene first-launch --at start` is the frame to check.

LANDSCAPE ONLY. In portrait the drawer is closed on this stage, so the only evidence on the plate is the `Index empty` pill at the very top — 2% of the frame, and portrait's tightest honoured window is 73.8%, which does not get near it. A format left out keeps the legacy move rather than pretending.

scenes.narration: Copy reference documents into the sources volume. Ingestion indexes them.

shots.alt: The field library sidebar listing thirty-two indexed documents grouped by category

WIDENED FROM 0.538 x 0.50 AT (0, 0) TO 0.82 x 0.70, measured with `ci-video focus-preview` against the committed plate.

The old note said "the same rectangle as `welcome-empty`, deliberately" — a before/after of one panel, framed identically so `0 chunks · 0 files` against `11,490 chunks · 32 files` is a comparison the viewer can actually make. That was the right intent, and #63 broke it without noticing: it widened `welcome-empty` to 0.82 x 0.70 to stop the frame edge slicing the hero, and left this shot on the rectangle it had just declared broken. The two shots have not been the same rectangle since, and the note claiming they were is how it stayed hidden.

WHAT IT LOOKED LIKE. A drift-down STARTS at its focus, and at 0.538 the start frame delivers plate x -0.001..0.562 against a hero block at x 0.425..0.765: "JUS", "Offline emergency knowledge, groun", "aid, water, shelter, power, commun", "answ" — four lines cut mid-glyph down the right canvas edge. Identical to the defect #63 wrote up on `welcome-empty`, on the plate one scene over.

(0, 0, 0.82, 0.70) -> scale 1.574, honoured exactly, window 0.820 square from plate (-0.001, -0.001). It ends past the hero paragraph at 0.765 so nothing is cut, `11,490 chunks · 32 files` and the `Ready · 32 docs` pill are both whole and legible at 1.57x, and the rectangle is once again character-for-character the one on `welcome-empty` — so the before/after is a real comparison again.

h 0.70 for the same reason it is 0.70 there: the window is square and sized by max(w, h), so h only moves the centre, and 0.70 keeps the window top above the plate rather than letting the caption-allowance offset slide it down onto the pill.

DRIFT-DOWN keeps its authored motion and still has room — 0.18 of plate below the window against the 0.063 it travels, so it is not the headroom-starved case that renders dead still while the storyboard claims it moves.

scenes.narration: The whole shelf stays browsable offline, on hardware you own.

shots.alt: The field library scrolled past its first categories, showing later category headers and their reference filenames with per-document chunk counts

WIDENED FROM 0.538 SQUARE AT (0, 0.187) TO 0.82 x 0.70 AT (0, 0), measured with `ci-video focus-preview` against the committed plate.

Same defect as `field-library` and for the same reason: any window tight enough to be honoured in 16:9 (0.538 is the floor, and on this plate it resolves to 0.606) starts at the left rail and therefore ends inside the hero block at plate x 0.425..0.765. scenes._transitionNote:
The cut out of the title card and into the product, and the first frame of the app in the film. `open` holds on the mark and the question "How long do you boil creek water?"; this scene answers a different question — what can you even ask it — and answers it with the app's own suggestions rather than with a claim. A dissolve would soften a boundary that wants to be hard: the argument stops and the product starts.

(It previously sat at the `first-run` -> `ask` chapter boundary and the note recorded that. The film no longer has a first-run section in front of the ask section, so the reason has changed even though the transition has not.)
scenes.caption: Water, burns, a 72-hour kit — before you type a word.
scenes.narration: First aid, power, water, food. The suggestions come from the shelf itself.

shots.alt: The six suggested questions the app offers on a ready appliance — purifying water, first aid for a burn, a seventy-two hour kit, treating a wound, wiring a solar panel to a battery, and preserving food without refrigeration
shots._shotNote:
These are the app's OWN suggestions (SUGGESTED_PROMPTS, public/app.js), not a list written for the video. That is the point: the breadth on screen is breadth the product actually has, and it moves when the product moves.

The corpus does NOT cover vehicle transportation, and device repair only through the iFixit ZIM — which is `_ftindex:no`, so it is browsable but cannot be retrieved from. Neither is claimed here, in the caption or the narration.
shots._focusNote:
RETARGETED — the rectangle this shot carried framed no chips at all. It was (0.171, 0.211), which resolves to a window over plate y 0.303..0.841 while both chip rows sit at 0.821..0.886. `ci-video focus-preview --scene what-you-can-ask` reconstructs the end frame as an empty dark rectangle with the chips sliced off along the bottom edge, under the caption band, i.e. the caption enumerated five subjects over a frame containing none of them. The prose note that used to sit here described a 0.65-wide rectangle at y 0.35; the numbers beside it were 0.538 at 0.211, so the note and the value had come apart at some point and the note was the thing being read.

The chip block is x 0.337..0.808 by y 0.821..0.886 — 0.47 on its longer side, under the 0.538 landscape floor, so 0.538 square is the tightest available and the shape of the block cannot be honoured. x 0.303 centres that square on the block (0.035 of margin left, 0.032 right, so no chip is clipped at either end — the clipped-'H' failure the old note describes is avoided by centring, not by widening).

y 0.462 IS THE MAXIMUM the plate allows: y + h must stay inside the screenshot, so the window is bottom-anchored at 0.462..1.0. That is also the only placement that clears the caption band — the chips land at 0.69 and 0.76 of canvas height and the band starts at ~0.85. Anything higher pushes the second row under the caption.

PUSH-IN, changed from drift-down, and forced: a bottom-anchored focus has zero headroomDown, so drift-down would hit the degradation path in cameraMove and silently become a push anyway. Declaring the push is honest, and it is the better move regardless — the shot opens wide and ends with the six questions filling the frame at the moment the cursor picks one.
shots._pointerNote:
The chip 'How do I purify water in the field?' — a real control, the app's own SUGGESTED_PROMPTS button, and the first subject the caption names ('Water'). Clicking it is also the film's argument: you can ask this thing without typing.

LANDSCAPE (0.400, 0.840): inside the pill, which spans x 0.337..0.482 by y 0.821..0.847 on the committed plate. Left of the pill's centre and low in it on purpose — the arrow's hotspot is its tip and its body hangs down-right, so this puts the body across the pill's lower edge instead of across the words. Inside the focus window (0.302..0.840 x 0.461..0.999), so the cursor is on canvas for the whole push rather than sliding off the end of it.

PORTRAIT (0.288, 0.830): the same chip on the mobile plate, where it spans x 0.032..0.545 by y 0.815..0.845. Centred, because a phone frame gets a tap ripple and a ripple has no body to keep off the label.

Both measured off the committed PNGs at 0.05 gridding, not derived from the landscape numbers — the app is responsive and the chip is 51% of the width on mobile against 15% on desktop.

scenes._prosodyNote: PIN REMOVED. It read "Pinned NEUTRAL to match the eleven tracks already in this film" — true when it was written, and false by the time this cut was assembled: eight of the thirteen lines here have since been recorded at the kit's per-kind register and only five were still neutral, so the pin was holding this scene to the minority. The whole set is now restyled together, which is what the old note said should happen and named the command for. Nothing about the words changed.
scenes._captionNote:
REWRITTEN FOR THE 9:16 CUT, and this is the second time this caption has been caught naming things that are not in the picture. It read "Water, burns, wounds, solar wiring, food — before you type a word", which is true of the LANDSCAPE plate: six chips, and all five subjects among them. The mobile plate renders three — `.chip-extra { display: none }` under 620px — and they are "How do I purify water in the field?", "First aid for a severe burn" and "Build a 72-hour emergency kit". So in the portrait cut the caption enumerated five subjects over a frame holding two of them. Verified against `suggestions.mobile.png`, not inferred from the CSS.

The three named now are the three chips that survive to portrait, so the caption is true of both cuts and no longer depends on which viewport the viewer got. The note this replaces recorded the same defect one revision earlier ("radio and navigation appear in no chip on screen") — the caption was fixed for the plate it was checked against and then not checked against the other one.

The narration is unchanged and is deliberately NOT the same list: "First aid, power, water, food. The suggestions come from the shelf itself." That sentence enumerates the SHELF, and says so in its second clause — power is NREL PV Solar Systems, food is Manual Of Gardening Bailey, both real rows in the library. A caption points at the frame; this line points at the corpus.

PORTRAIT (0.760, 0.930): the mobile input spans x 0.028..0.865 by y 0.902..0.958 and the typed text stops at 0.68, so this is the same idea on the phone plate — clear of the words, well inside the field, and clear of the Send button at 0.885..0.975.
shots._focusNote:
NO FOCUS IN EITHER FORMAT, and this one is a measured refusal rather than an omission.

The subject is the composer at plate y 0.898..0.955 — the bottom 7% of the screenshot. scenes._transitionNote: Forced by the focus on the scene before it, and measured rather than assumed. Both scenes now end full-bleed on the same app screen at nearly the same scale, and the default half-second cross-dissolve between them renders as two full-frame copies of the answer text sliding through each other — a screenful of overlapping body copy that reads as a broken render, not a transition. At rest the same dissolve was harmless, because both plates were small cards on a lot of empty ground. AUTHORING.md predicts this ('a cross-dissolve between two shots of the SAME app screen reads as a double-exposure ghost'); punching in is what makes it unmissable. Cut instead — which is also the right edit, since this is the escalation from the answer to its receipts.

scenes.narration: See exactly which documents the answer came from. Verify before you act.

shots.alt: The expanded sources accordion listing the documents the answer was drawn from — two field manuals and, marked as encyclopedia, a Wikipedia article served from the offline ZIM library — each with the passage that matched
shots._focusNote:
MEASURED WITH `ci-video focus-preview` AND AGAINST THE RENDERED CUT, 2026-08-12. Retargeted from 0.538 square at (0.227, 0.195), and the motion changed with it.

WHAT WAS WRONG. The old window delivered plate x 0.226..0.764 by y 0.287..0.825 at the end of the drift. The Wikipedia row — `wikipedia_en_simple_all_nopic — Boiling  ENCYCLOPEDIA  match 2%`, which is the ONLY on-screen proof for the NEXT scene's caption, "No connection. Wikipedia, on the box, in the answers." — landed at canvas y 0.73. The caption scrim's gradient starts at canvas 0.720 and is solid from 0.853, so the row and its snippet rendered under the scrim, greyed to the point of illegibility. That is how this was found: in the delivered frame, not in the reconstruction, which draws no scrim. Every card was also cut off at the right edge mid-sentence, because the cards run to plate x 0.850 and the window stopped at 0.764.

THE FIX IS TO LET THE SOURCES LIST BE THE WHOLE SHOT. (0.314, 0.35, 0.56, 0.50) -> scale 2.304, honoured exactly, window 0.560 square from plate (0.313, 0.350). The three cards span plate x 0.339..0.850 by y 0.426..0.740, so they sit inside it with margin at both ends: nothing is cut at the right edge, the Wikipedia row lands at canvas y 0.58 and its last snippet line at 0.66 — both clear of the scrim. y 0.35 rather than 0.36-0.40 so the window top falls just ABOVE the answer card's last line instead of through it; at 0.36 that line is sliced in half along the top edge, which is the same defect one edge over.

PUSH-IN, changed from drift-down, and the reason is arithmetic rather than taste. The pointer sits on the SOURCES triangle at plate y 0.421 and the last card ends at 0.740 — 0.319 of plate that must be held between a top margin the cursor needs and the scrim line at canvas 0.72, i.e. inside 0.70 x 0.56 = 0.392 of plate. A drift-down adds its 0.063 of travel to that requirement (0.410) and it no longer fits: every candidate y either drops the cursor off the top edge by the end or pushes the Wikipedia snippet back under the scrim. The drift existed because the old window could not hold three cards at once; this one can, so there is nothing left to travel through.

LANDSCAPE ONLY, unchanged. On mobile the source list is full-bleed body copy that is already comfortable to read, so the only portrait framing available would crop the card text at the sides. A format left out keeps the legacy move.

scenes._transitionNote: The chapter boundary — `first-run` ends and `offline` begins — and the hardest subject change in the film: the three scenes before it build a shelf, this one takes the network away and shows that nothing on that shelf moved. The three first-run beats dissolve into each other because they are one continuous section; the cut is what marks the section ending. (It was authored as a ghost guard against `check-the-sources`, which used to precede it and ended full-bleed on the same app screen at the same scale. That neighbour has changed. `library-shelf` ends at 1.574 and this scene opens at 1.0, so there is no double exposure to guard against any more — the cut is now punctuation on its own account.)
scenes.caption: No connection. Wikipedia, on the box, in the answers.
scenes.narration: The network is gone and nothing changes. The encyclopedia is on the box too.

shots.alt: The appliance with a ZIM library mounted: the System panel reads Encyclopedia, three archives, beside the local index, and the sidebar footer reads Runs 100% offline
shots._shotNote: Captured with EVERY external request blocked and recorded — see the egress guard in capture.config.mjs. If this app ever fetches a font, a script or a beacon, the capture fails instead of quietly filming a product that phones home under a narration saying it does not. The offline claim in this film is enforced, not asserted.
shots._focusNote:
Lands on the System panel, where the two facts this scene asserts are actually written: ENCYCLOPEDIA / 3 archives, and the footer's offline dot. At rest they are ~11px on a 1080-tall canvas — legible on a desktop monitor, not in a 16:9 video.

0.54 SQUARE IS DELIBERATE, and was measured with `ci-video focus-preview` rather than guessed. An earlier 0.42x0.50 asked for scale 3.0, clamped to the 2.4 ceiling, and past the ceiling the rectangle stops being read at all — moving its centre changes nothing, so the framing was the kit's rather than mine. 0.54 gives the same picture at scale 2.34, under control, and leaves the window free to sit against the left canvas edge where the sidebar is.

LANDSCAPE ONLY. In portrait the sidebar is off-canvas below 920px (style.css) and the drawer eval opens it full-bleed, so the panel is already large and a crop would only slice it. A format left out keeps the legacy move, which is the right answer when a screen does not need a camera on 9:16.

scenes._transitionNote: Two reasons, one of them measured. The subject changes hard — the scene before is about the network being gone while everything still works, this one is about the language model being absent, a different failure and a different panel. And with this scene now opening full-bleed on the banner while `no-network` ends full-bleed on the System panel, the default half-second dissolve would cross two copies of the same app screen at nearly the same scale: the double-exposure ghost AUTHORING.md names, and the same one that already forced cuts on `check-the-sources` and `no-network`. Changing the motion here is what created the hazard, so the cut goes in with it rather than after somebody screenshots it.
scenes.caption: No model on the box? It says so, and keeps going.
scenes.narration: With no language model installed it says so, and the library stays browsable.

shots.alt: The degraded state: an LLM missing status pill and a banner naming the directory the model files belong in
shots._focusNote:
PULL-BACK IS THE CAPTION. 'It says so, and keeps going' is two beats in order: open on the thing that says so — the `LLM missing` pill and the banner naming /app/gguf_models — then pull back to the appliance with its thirty-two documents still listed underneath. A push-in would have run the sentence backwards.

LANDSCAPE 0.62 wide, not the 0.538 floor, because the banner runs x 0.203..0.813 and a 0.538 window slices it mid-sentence. Half a sentence in frame is worse than 13% less magnification, and the whole point of the shot is that the app tells you what to do. x 0.195 puts the window at 0.194..0.814 — both ends of the banner inside it with a pixel to spare. h 0.58 is doing the same job h 0.5 does on `welcome-empty`: it only moves the window's centre, and at 0.58 the window starts at plate 0.014 so the status pill (0.021..0.045) is whole rather than sliced by the caption-allowance offset. scale lands at 2.081, honoured exactly, no clamp. Verified with `ci-video focus-preview`.

PORTRAIT w 1.0 asks for nothing tighter than full-bleed, which is the only thing worth asking for on this plate: the banner wraps to three lines running x 0.02..0.95, so any window narrower than the plate cuts words off both ends, and portrait's floor is 73.8%. What the declaration buys is the coverScale reframe the `answer` shot uses — the phone frame drops away and the screen grows 39%, which is the whole legibility gain available here. h 0.62 keeps the centre high so the window anchors to the top of the plate where the banner is.

scenes._narrationNote: The line used to be "One Docker stack. No accounts, no cloud. It keeps working when the network does not." — whose first seven words were the caption, verbatim, read aloud while the caption was on screen. The voice now spends that time on the only thing this scene has left to say. The three nouns are the film's own arc in order — the shelf, the typed question, the cited answer — so the recap recaps something the viewer watched rather than introducing a fourth claim in the last six seconds.
scenes._itemsNote:
MESSAGING.md's "ownership tally". `Monthly fee - $0` gave up its slot to `Encyclopedia - On disk` when the ZIM library landed: four chips fit one landscape row and five wrap, and of the five candidates the price is the one the outro's own argument already implies while the encyclopedia is a capability the viewer has just watched being cited.

`Data leaves home - Never` is a claim, so it was verified rather than assumed, because the fleet review caught this exact chip being false on Spellbook. CMakeLists.txt defaults JIC_SENTRY OFF, the Dockerfile defaults ARG JIC_SENTRY=0 and in that state links no Sentry code at all, and docker-publish.yml passes no build-args. It is now ALSO enforced at capture time by the egress guard in video/capture.config.mjs.

scenes.narration: Just In Case, from Companion Intelligence. UnCloud your life.
scenes._transitionNote: A hold, and it is doing two jobs. Editorially it is the last breath of the film: the four tally chips land, the frame goes to bare ground for `meta.holdSeconds`, and the CTA arrives on its own. Mechanically it removes the only overlap `check` flags in either format — at a cross-dissolve the recap chips were still on screen across the CTA at t=64.08s, reported as content_overlap in both cuts, because `reveal: "paced"` now spreads four chips across a 6.1s read and the last of them lands inside the dissolve. A hold is the fix that is also the better edit.
